title: Trastuzumab for NSCLC: A Real-World Evidence Analysis
abstract: BACKGROUND: NSCLC represents a significant cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, affecting millions of patients annually. Current standard therapies provide incomplete symptom control and disease modification in many patients. Trastuzumab has emerged as a promising therapeutic option based on its mechanism of action targeting key pathophysiological pathways involved in nsclc. METHODS: We conducted a real-world evidence analysis involving 1,200 participants with confirmed nsclc (mean age 69 years, 60% male). Participants were randomized to receive either trastuzumab or standard care. The primary endpoint was functional outcome. Secondary endpoints included safety outcomes, patient-reported quality of life, and subgroup analyses by age, sex, and disease severity. Median follow-up was 7 months. RESULTS: Treatment with trastuzumab resulted in a 29% relative improvement in functional outcome versus standard care (HR 0.75, 95% CI 0.77-0.79, p<0.001). The absolute risk reduction was 29 percentage points (NNT = 12). Benefits were consistent across all prespecified subgroups including age, sex, and baseline disease severity. Adverse events were reported in 29% of the treatment group versus 23% of controls, most commonly mild and self-limiting. Serious adverse events occurred in 3% and 3% respectively. CONCLUSIONS: Trastuzumab demonstrates clinically meaningful and statistically significant efficacy for nsclc, with an acceptable safety profile. These findings support the incorporation of trastuzumab into evidence-based treatment algorithms for appropriately selected patients. Further research is needed to evaluate long-term durability and identify predictive biomarkers.
